The running head 'Outer None / Divine Name None' is harmless in a comparison preview.

Thursday commentary: in documentary-hebrew PDF 101 (note 104) and documentary PDF 289 (note 139) it is set whole on the page of its target line, with the נ״א note (105 / 140) after it. Headings: סדר תשליך, שיר היחוד ליום ראשון…השבת and שיר הכבוד all start cleanly. No heading is stranded at the bottom of a page (e.g. ליום חמישי at the top of PDF 99 / 287, ליום השבת mid-page on PDF 103 / 291). Mini documentary-optional-false p9–16: Wednesday and Thursday flow with no large blank gaps and no empty bracketed rows. Mini expanded-wednesday shows only the Wednesday hymn plus שיר הכבוד, then metadata.
The overfull \vbox warnings did not show up as visible clipping, overlap or overflow on any page I inspected.
Footnote markers in the poetry are set as small numbers between lines at the right edge (e.g. 101, 136, 141). Pre-existing note 98 on PDF 90 is set the same way, so this is house style, not a defect.

Expanded profile only: the appendix carries English editorial headings ('Supplementary hymns', 'Hymn of Divine Unity — Sunday…Shabbat', 'Hymn of Glory'). These are structural labels, not translations of the poems, so I don't count them as added translation. Confirm they are intended if that matters for the English-context policy.

The missing-opener note reads 'Supplied delimiter: (' while the rendered line shows the exporter's [ ] optional brackets. This is accurate about the source, but a reader may briefly wonder why the note says '(' and the line shows '['. It is optional wording polish, not a required change.
Metadata pages (documentary-hebrew PDF 105–107, expanded PDF 350–352) render cleanly: licences, credits, sources (Heidenheim–Marmorstein, plus Birnbaum in expanded) and the genizah notice.
